title: Some and any
summary: Тонкости some и any: some в вопросах-предложениях, any в утверждениях (любой), any после hardly / without / if, some с единственным числом (some man) и с цифрами (some 200 people), someone / anyone и ударные формы.
ru:
## Базовое правило и где оно ломается
В учебнике вы видели схему: **some** — в утверждениях, **any** — в вопросах и отрицаниях. Это только приблизительное правило. В реальной речи выбор зависит от того, **что имеет в виду говорящий**.
> I have **some** questions. — У меня есть вопросы.
> I don't have **any** questions. — У меня нет вопросов.
> Do you have **any** questions? — У вас есть вопросы? (нейтральный, не знаем, есть ли)
> Would you like **some** coffee? — Хотите кофе? (предложение, ожидается «да»)

## some в вопросах: предложения и просьбы
В вопросах, где говорящий **ожидает положительный ответ** или что-то предлагает, ставят **some**:
> Would you like **some** tea? — Хотите чаю? (предлагаем, ожидаем «да»)
> Could you lend me **some** money? — Не могли бы вы одолжить мне денег? (просьба)
> Did **somebody** call? — Кто-нибудь звонил? (мы думаем, что да)
> Can I have **some** water? — Можно мне воды?
С **any** вопрос становится нейтральным или сомневающимся: *Do you have **any** change?* — Есть ли у вас мелочь? (не знаю, есть ли).

## any в утверждениях: «любой»
В утвердительных предложениях **any** (ударное, [ˈeni]) значит **«любой, какой угодно»**: *Any teacher can tell you that. Take any book you like. You can ask anyone.* Это не то же самое, что **some**: *Some teachers can tell you* — некоторые.
> **Any** child would enjoy this game. — Любому ребёнку понравится эта игра.
> You can choose **any** colour. — Можете выбрать любой цвет.
> **Anybody** could have done it. — Это мог сделать кто угодно.

## any после «отрицательных» слов
**Any** появляется после слов с негативным или ограничивающим смыслом, даже если сам глагол в утвердительной форме: **hardly, barely, scarcely, never, rarely, seldom, without, refuse, deny, fail, before, too, if, whether**:
> There is **hardly any** time left. — Почти не осталось времени.
> He left **without any** explanation. — Он ушёл без всяких объяснений.
> **If** you have **any** doubts, ask me. — Если у вас есть какие-то сомнения, спросите меня.
> I **doubt** that she has **any** idea. — Сомневаюсь, что она вообще что-то понимает.
> I'm too tired to do **anything**. — Я слишком устал, чтобы что-то делать.
> **Before any** decision is made, we need the data. — Прежде чем принимать решение...

## some с единственным числом и с числами
- **some + ед. число** = «какой-то (неизвестный)»: *Some man called for you.* — Вам звонил какой-то человек. *She moved to some small town in Ohio.*
- **some + число** = «около»: *Some 300 people attended.* — Около 300 человек. (формально)
- **some of + the/these/my**: *some of the students, some of my colleagues, some of it*.
- **any of** + мн. число / the: *Did any of the guests arrive?*

## somebody / anybody, something / anything
Правила те же: **-some-** в утверждениях и предложениях, **-any-** в отрицаниях, вопросах и в смысле «кто/что угодно».
> **Somebody** has left the door open. — Кто-то оставил дверь открытой.
> I didn't tell **anyone**. — Я никому не сказал.
> Is there **anything** I can do? — Могу я чем-то помочь?
> **Anything** is better than nothing. — Что угодно лучше, чем ничего.
Глаголы после these слов обычно в ед. числе, а местоимения — **they / them / their**: *Somebody left **their** umbrella.*

## any и сравнение, any more
- **any + сравнительная степень** (в вопросах и отрицаниях): *Is it any better? It isn't any cheaper.*
- **any more / anymore** — «больше не»: *He doesn't live here **any more**.* В американском английском часто одним словом: *anymore*.

## Типичные ошибки
- ~~I don't have some money.~~ → I don't have **any** money.
- ~~There is hardly some time left.~~ → There is hardly **any** time left.
- ~~Any man called for you.~~ (хотели сказать «кто-то») → **Some** man called for you.
- ~~I can't see nobody.~~ → I can't see **anybody**. / I can see **nobody**.
en:
## The basic rule and where it breaks
You have seen the simple scheme: **some** in positive sentences, **any** in questions and negatives. That is only an approximation. In real speech the choice depends on **what the speaker means**.
> I have **some** questions.
> I don't have **any** questions.
> Do you have **any** questions? (neutral: we do not know)
> Would you like **some** coffee? (an offer; we expect 'yes')

## some in questions: offers and requests
In questions where the speaker **expects 'yes'** or makes an offer, we use **some**:
> Would you like **some** tea?
> Could you lend me **some** money?
> Did **somebody** call? (we think so)
> Can I have **some** water?
With **any** the question is neutral or doubtful: *Do you have **any** change?* (I do not know whether you do).

## any in positive sentences: 'it doesn't matter which'
In positive sentences, stressed **any** [ˈeni] means **'no matter which'**: *Any teacher can tell you that. Take any book you like. You can ask anyone.* It is not the same as **some**: *Some teachers can tell you* means 'a few'.
> **Any** child would enjoy this game.
> You can choose **any** colour.
> **Anybody** could have done it.

## any after 'negative' words
**Any** appears after words with a negative or limiting meaning, even when the verb is positive: **hardly, barely, scarcely, never, rarely, seldom, without, refuse, deny, fail, before, too, if, whether, doubt**:
> There is **hardly any** time left.
> He left **without any** explanation.
> **If** you have **any** doubts, ask me.
> I **doubt** that she has **any** idea.
> I'm too tired to do **anything**.

## some + singular noun and some + number
- **some + singular** = 'an unknown': *Some man called for you.* *She moved to some small town in Ohio.*
- **some + number** = 'about': *Some 300 people attended.* (formal)
- **some of + the/these/my**: *some of the students, some of my colleagues, some of it*.
- **any of** + plural / the: *Did any of the guests arrive?*

## somebody / anybody, something / anything
The same rules: **-some-** in positive statements and offers, **-any-** in negatives, questions and the sense of 'it doesn't matter who/what'.
> **Somebody** has left the door open.
> I didn't tell **anyone**.
> Is there **anything** I can do?
> **Anything** is better than nothing.
The verb is singular, but the pronouns are normally **they / them / their**: *Somebody left **their** umbrella.*

## any + comparative, any more
- **any + comparative** (in questions and negatives): *Is it any better? It isn't any cheaper.*
- **any more / anymore** = 'no longer': *He doesn't live here **any more**.* In American English often written as one word.

## Common mistakes
- ~~I don't have some money.~~ → I don't have **any** money.
- ~~There is hardly some time left.~~ → There is hardly **any** time left.
- ~~Any man called for you.~~ (meaning 'a certain man') → **Some** man called for you.
- ~~I can't see nobody.~~ → I can't see **anybody**. / I can see **nobody**.
structure:
## Основные значения
| Контекст | Слово | Пример |
|---|---|---|
| утверждение | some | I bought **some** apples. |
| отрицание | any | I didn't buy **any** apples. |
| нейтральный вопрос | any | Did you buy **any** apples? |
| предложение / просьба | some | Would you like **some** apples? |
| любой (ударное any) | any | **Any** apple will do. |
| после hardly, without, if | any | There's hardly **any** left. |

## Производные
| some- | any- | no- |
|---|---|---|
| somebody / someone | anybody / anyone | nobody / no one |
| something | anything | nothing |
| somewhere | anywhere | nowhere |

## Особые значения some
| Значение | Пример |
|---|---|
| какой-то (неизвестный) | **Some** guy asked about you. |
| около (формально) | **Some** 50 people attended. |
| некоторые (противопоставление) | **Some** people like it; others don't. |

## Особые значения any
> **any** + comparative: *Is she **any** better?*
> **any more**: *I don't smoke **any more**.*
> **if any**: *Correct the mistakes, **if any**.*

exercises.title: some или any?
exercises.instruction: Вставьте **some, any** или производное слово (**somebody, anybody, something, anything** и т. д.).
exercises.example: I didn't see ___ mistakes. → I didn't see **any** mistakes.

items.text: There's hardly {{any}} milk left in the fridge.
I'm sure {{somebody|someone}} has already told her.
He left the meeting without saying {{anything}}.
If you have {{any}} questions, please contact the office.
Could you give me {{some}} advice about the contract?
She refused to give us {{any}} details.
I'm too tired to cook {{anything}} tonight.

exercises.title: any (любой), some (какой-то) или any more
exercises.instruction: Вставьте **any, some, anyone, someone** или **anymore / any more**. Если допустимо несколько вариантов, перечислите их.

items.text: {{Any}} student can borrow books from the library; you just need a card.
{{Some}} man was asking about you at the reception.
I don't think the new software is {{any}} better than the old one.
{{Anyone|Anybody}} can learn to swim if they practise.
We need to correct all the errors, if {{any}}.

items.q: Would you like ___ help with that?
I haven't made ___ progress this week.
There is hardly ___ chance that she will win.
items.why: hardly делает предложение отрицательным по смыслу: any.

items.q: ___ one of these tools will do the job.
I'm sure there is ___ in the fridge that we can eat.
Is the new model ___ faster than the old one?
items.why: any + сравнительная степень в вопросе и отрицании: any faster.

items.q: I didn't meet ___ interesting at the conference.

options: Could I have some water, please?
Could I have any water, please?
Could I have somewhat water, please?

items.why: Для неизвестного человека — their (единственное число они).

options: There is hardly some bread left.
There is hardly any bread left.
There is hardly no bread left.
I will do any for you.
I will do anything for you.
I will do something any for you.

exercises.title: Перепишите предложение
exercises.instruction: Перепишите предложение, используя слово в скобках.

items.prompt: There was almost no traffic. (hardly) → There was ...
He left and said nothing. (without) → He left ...
answers: He left without saying a word.

items.prompt: Offer a guest some tea. (Would) → Would ...
It doesn't matter which book you take. (any) → You can take ...
She no longer works here. (any more) → She doesn't ...
answers: She doesn't work here any more.

items.prompt: I don't know the people in the room. (anybody) → I don't ...
answers: I don't know anybody in the room.
I don't know anyone in the room.

exercises.title: Исправьте ошибки
exercises.instruction: В каждом предложении есть ошибка с some или any. Перепишите предложение верно.

items.prompt: I can't find some of my keys anywhere.
answers: I can't find any of my keys anywhere.

items.prompt: I didn't buy some bread this morning.
answers: I didn't buy any bread this morning.
I did not buy any bread this morning.

items.prompt: There is hardly some difference between them.
answers: There is hardly any difference between them.

items.prompt: Any man called for you while you were out. (какой-то незнакомый)
answers: Some man called for you while you were out.

items.prompt: She didn't tell something to anybody.
answers: She didn't tell anything to anybody.
She didn't tell anything to anyone.

items.prompt: If you have some problems, let me know.
answers: If you have any problems, let me know.

items.prompt: Что бы вы предложили гостю? (Would you like some ...?)
items.sample: Would you like some tea or coffee?

items.prompt: Что вы никогда не едите или не делаете? (never ... any)
items.sample: I never eat any meat because I'm a vegetarian.

items.prompt: Скажите о том, что может сделать любой человек (Anyone can ...).
items.sample: Anyone can learn a new language if they are patient.

items.prompt: Что вы сделали бы без чьей-то помощи? (without any ...)
items.sample: I finished the project without any help from my team.
